items.text: The sleeve repairs are finished. Our conservation team will send you the matching condition cards tomorrow, and the cards will include the treatment photographs.
Last winter I promised to send the tape inventory by the end of that week. I am recounting the old arrangement here.
I will send you the accession packets for the dune-grass seeds tomorrow.
I can export the piano's voicing records as a PDF. That describes the workshop software's capability; I have not set a delivery date.
The grower hopes to finish her orchard ledger next month. I will send you our completed cooperative graft ledger tomorrow.
Our plan is to send the concert piano's voicing log at noon on Friday. To be explicit, we will do so.
We will send the course sketches when the wind survey is ready. The survey team has not finished its measurements.
I repaired the split hem yesterday and handed the revised condition card to the registrar. The treatment entry now includes the thread specification.
The inventory I sent in June covered only interview tapes. I will deliver the music-tape inventory this Friday.
I previously wrote, "We will deliver the cue sheets on Monday." Please disregard that assurance; we now hope to send them later in the week.
If the wind survey is ready tonight, I will get you the course sketches before tomorrow's launch.
You asked for the entrance map. I will send you the final cartographic plate tomorrow morning.
I withdraw my promise to send the granite catalogue tomorrow. I will send you the limestone sample catalogue tomorrow.
The donor's earlier dispatch covered the seed jars only. You will receive the matching accession envelopes from our curation team by noon tomorrow.
I will not deliver the restoration cue sheets tomorrow; that earlier assurance was a mistake.
I delivered the community radio tape inventory last Tuesday.
The donor wrote, "I will send the accession envelopes on Thursday." I am recording her words here so the intake desk knows what she said.
Before the first kite launches, you will have the printed course sketches from our organising team. Each sheet includes the recovery lane.
Yesterday I dispatched the accession packets for all twelve meadow collections. Their tracking slips are attached to the intake log.
You will receive the completed tapestry condition cards from me by Thursday afternoon.
I will deliver the regatta course sketches before the opening briefing.
If the quarry manager approves the sample list, I will send both catalogues on Friday. Without that approval, neither will be sent.
You may find my tonal annotations conservative. Still, I can promise that I will deliver the voicing records tomorrow.
The cooling delay concerns the new bell. For the tested bell, our team will be handing over the signed acoustic certificate at 10 tomorrow.
Mara, the grower, told me, "We will send the graft ledger on Monday." Her 'we' refers to the nursery staff.
My earlier note incorrectly promised both reels. I will send the completed cue sheet for reel one on Friday. Reel two has no delivery date.
If the bronze has cooled enough for the resonance test, we will deliver the acoustic certificate on Tuesday. The cooling rate is still uncertain.
Could you send me the annotated cave-survey plates before the archive meeting?
At 9 tomorrow morning, we will be handing over the updated tape inventory to the station librarian.
Please enter the display-case numbers on the textile condition cards and return them to me.
My coordination team owns the consolidated graft ledger. We will deliver it to you on Monday.
Our archive team will deliver the western-passage map plates to you at Friday's briefing; the cartographer's forecast concerns the separate eastern survey.
I intend to send you the voicing records on Wednesday.
Friday's handover: I will send the limestone catalogue; the granite catalogue will follow if the sample review passes. That condition applies to the catalogue delivery.
The expedition cartographer expects her team to deliver the eastern-chamber plates next week. That is her forecast, copied into my archive notes.
The bell is still in the cooling pit. I will send its acoustic certificate when the casting is cool enough to test.
To correct the record: I can promise that you will receive the corrected cue sheets tomorrow. My retraction concerned the restored picture master.
The grower has a separate ledger for her pear grafts. She says she will deliver it on Thursday. I have only copied that statement into the cooperative's notes.
At Monday's inspection, I will hand you the acoustic certificate for bell B17.
You will receive the sandstone sample catalogue from our estimating team by noon Monday. The slate catalogue is no longer promised for that date.
